:::{#sol-rank-subadditive-practice}

In $\matr{A}$, the second [column](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column) is twice the first,
so $\rankf{\matr{A}} = 1$.
In $\matr{B}$, the first column is $\vzero_2$
and the second is not,
so $\rankf{\matr{B}} = 1$.
Then

$$
\matr{A} + \matr{B} = \sbmat{1 & 3 \\ 2 & 7}.
$$

Its [columns](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix-column) are [linearly independent](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-linearly-independent):
$c_1\,(1, 2) + c_2\,(3, 7) = \vzero_2$ gives $c_1 = -3 c_2$ from the first entry,
and then $-6 c_2 + 7 c_2 = c_2 = 0$ from the second.
So $\rankf{\matr{A} + \matr{B}} = 2 = 1 + 1$,
and @thm-rank-subadditive holds with equality.

:::
